The Immigrant Legal Resource Center is Hiring!

StaffAttorney - San Joaquin Valley Central Valley of California The Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC) is seeking a full-time Staff Attorney working remotely from the San Joaquin Valley of California.Applicants living adjacent to the San Joaquin Valley and willing to travel to the San Joaquin Valley on a weekly basis may be considered.

For purposes of this announcement, the San Joaquin Valley consists of the following eight counties: Fresno, Kern, Kings, Madera, Merced, San Joaquin, Stanislaus, and Tulare.This is an exempt position that reports to a Directing Attorney. This is a bargaining unit position represented by the National Legal Services Workers (NOLSW), Local 2320.

Who We Are:  The ILRC is a leading immigrant rights organization headquartered in San Francisco with staff in Washington, D.C., Texas, Southern California, the Central Valley of California, and Washington state.

Since 1979, our mission has been to educate, support, and empower immigrants, community organizations, and legal practitioners to build a more just, inclusive, and democratic society. Our team is passionate, collaborative, and committed to equity and innovation in all we do. Additional information about our organizational values is available here.

The Opportunity:  Thisposition offers an opportunity to join a mission-driven team dedicated to strengthening the ecosystem of organizations providing family-based affirmative and removal defense services within the San Joaquin Valley.

The ideal candidate will help build the capacity of local partners by delivering legal trainings, providing technical assistance, supporting communitymembers directly at legal workshops, and developing clear, accessible community resourcesand practice advisories for legal practitioners.

The ideal candidate will also participate in key collaboratives, networks, and coalitions to share resources, provide timely updates, and advance pro-immigrant efforts across the region. Job Responsibilities:The Staff Attorney- San Joaquin Valley will contribute to several concurrent programs.

Duties may include: Conducting in-person and/or webinartrainings on immigration law and practice for attorneys and accredited representatives. Providing training to community members in English and Spanish on a variety of immigration law topics, including Know Your Rights and Public Charge.

Providing legal review and advice at immigration workshops on various topics. Participating in regional collaboratives and task forces to represent the ILRC and provide relevant information on immigrant rights, immigration law, and policy updates.

Traveling for trainings, meetings, and other events throughout the San Joaquin Valley, the rest of California, and, at times, throughout the United States. Contributing to ILRClegal projects, including writing, editing, and updating legal manuals and publications.

Conducting caserounds and providing case-specific technical assistance to nonprofit agency staff, private practice attorneys, and pro bono attorneys in the region who work with low-income noncitizens on various areas of family-based defensive and affirmative immigration law.

Ability to present accessible information in English and Spanish to on complex legal topics to the media, community members, and practitioners.

Required Qualifications:  The successful applicant is required to have: A minimum of 5 years of experience representing clients in the practice of general immigration law includingrepresenting clients before USCIS, EOIR, and the BIA; Broad knowledge of immigration law, including the grounds of inadmissibility and deportability and eligibility for relief; Strong foundation in removal defense practice, federal court litigation, and legal responses to immigration enforcement; Ability to lead meetings and communicate with a range of people, including attorneys, community members, advocates, policy-makers, funders, and others; Willing to work closely with and learn from colleagues, including being willing to take direction and editing from others and to incorporate feedback;   Excellent writing, editing, and legal analysis skills;  Excellent training and presentation skills;  Strong time management skills and the ability to meet deadlines;  A strong work ethic, including the following qualities: organized, flexible, reliable, and dependable, able to work independently, and able to handle several projects simultaneously;  Willing to participate in team-based efforts and a collaborative decision-making environment;  A current bar membership in good standing for any state in the United States or the District of Columbia, although California is preferred; and, Demonstrated proficiency in Spanish, including strong speaking and writing skills.

Preferred Qualifications: Engagement with rapid response networks and urgent legal response strategies. Technical writing for immigration or other purposes. Training, teaching, or other public speaking experience. Working in, leading, or forming coalitions. Collaborating with organizers, advocates, and immigrant communities.

Compensation/Benefits:   Pay is extremely competitive for the field and commensurate with experience according to the ILRC salary scale for attorneys. The starting pay for this position is$93,509.70for those who are 5years out of law school.

An attorney hired for this position who has been out of law school for more than 5 years will have a higher salary based on their law school graduation year.

For instance, an attorney who has been out of law school for 10 years would have a salary of$116,008.70.The ILRC offers excellent benefits, medical/dental/vision insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) sessions, a flexible spending account for medical and dependent care, vacation, and sick leave.

The ILRC also sponsors a retirement plan contribution upon fulfillment of eligibility. Additionally, we offer an annual professional development stipend of $2,500 and, from 2024 – 2027, an annual wellness stipend of $2,500.

ILRC also offers a sabbatical program: employees are eligible to apply for an 8-week sabbatical after five years of service and a 12-week sabbatical after ten years of service. Applications:  This position will remain open until it is filled and is currently available. We will consider applications on an ongoing basis beginning immediately.

To ensure consideration of your application, please submit a cover letter explaining your qualifications for the position, your salary requirements, a current resume, a writing sample that demonstrates immigration and criminal law knowledge, and the contact information for three professional references, one of which must be a supervisor.

About Checkr

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company .

Reporting to Checkr’s VP, Commercial & Corporate Legal, you’ll join our legal team as Commercial Counsel and serve as a trusted advisor to the revenue organization on the agreements that power our growth.

You’ll draft, negotiate, and close a wide range of complex, enterprise-level commercial agreements, advising internal clients on the legal, regulatory, and risk considerations behind each deal.

Partnering closely with Sales and Revenue, and cross-functionally with Compliance, you’ll help Checkr scale responsibly and move deals at the speed our customers expect.

· Lead the review, drafting, and negotiation of a variety of commercial agreements, including SaaS, licensing, partnership, and data provider agreements

· Research and analyze laws that affect the business, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), from a commercial standpoint

· Partner cross-functionally as a creative problem-solver and strategic thinker, and help manage outside counsel on commercial matters

· JD and active membership in good standing of the California Bar

· 3+ years of experience structuring, drafting, and negotiating commercial agreements, ideally with some time in-house at a high-growth technology company

· Working knowledge of the legal issues in commercial agreements—liability, indemnification, risk allocation, data protection, privacy—and the judgment to know when risks matter and when to consult subject-matter experts (including on the FCRA)

· A pragmatic strategist who resolves issues in the context of the company’s commercial goals and risk thresholds and communicates them clearly to non-lawyers, including senior stakeholders

· Ability to manage many projects independently in a fast-paced environment, with strong attention to detail, sound judgment, humility, and a good sense of humor

Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people.

The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter.

By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

We are looking for an innovative and curious Corporate Counsel to help shape how Elastic’s technologies are built, protected, and brought to market.

Elastic is distributed-by-design and this role can be located in the United States or Canada, reporting to the Vice President of Legal Innovation (Product, IP, Marketing) with dotted line supervision by the Director of Legal Innovation.

You will work alongside product and engineering teams from initial ideation through product launch, supporting legal design advice on features at the cutting edge of enterprise technology, helping the company to scale at velocity. The role assists with day-to-day in-house innovation and patent prosecution management.

It carries a broad set of additional product counsel responsibilities collaborating with other legal team members to address AI governance, open-source licensing, dependency management, trademark and brand protection, baseline trade compliance backup, and commercial enablement.

We're looking for a resourceful early career attorney with a roll-up-your-sleeves demeanor and the ability to navigate the intersection of law and emerging technology.
What You Will Be Doing
This is a dynamic role for a proactive advocate who enjoys finding solutions and bringing velocity to quality outcomes. In this capacity, you will:
Patent Prosecution & Invention Harvesting: Support Elastic's day-to-day patent prosecution and innovation motions. Develop a deep working knowledge of Elastic's product technology and roadmap.

Assist in operating the invention harvesting and patent intake program by working with other Elasticians to identify innovative ideas, evaluate inventions for patentability, and prepare or review patent disclosures.

You will support and assist more senior legal team members and stakeholders in working with outside patent counsel, help identify and prioritize IP filings in line with portfolio strategy, and support value creation and efficiencies in IP portfolio management.
IP Portfolio Management: Working closely with the Director of Legal for Product and IP, help manage Elastic's global patent, copyright, and trademark portfolios, including trademark monitoring and clearance, copyright registrations, and tracking all filing, prosecution, and renewal deadlines across jurisdictions.
Brand Protection & Enforcement: Support IP enforcement strategies by assisting with domain name disputes, social media takedowns, and coordination with vendors and outside counsel on pre-litigation disputes and assertions.
Product Regulatory Governance & Product Launch Readiness: Coordinate with cross-functional team members, including Legal Privacy and Commercial, Information Security, and IT to support our Product build and release functions. Support ongoing improvements to related internal guidelines as necessary to ensure all Elasticians are operating efficiently and effectively within the productization and go-to-market functions.
Open-Source & Product Counseling: Assist in managing day-to-day open-source software licensing and compliance programs, ensuring inbound third-party dependencies align with our outbound strategy. Support in the creation of advice and assistance for engineering and product management teams on intellectual property rights, open-source licensing, AI modelopen weight licensing, dependencies generally, and data collection/usage risks.
Commercial Contracts & Playbooks: Review, research, and prepare first drafts of commercial contract clauses related to AI, IP, Product, dependencies, and open-source software—including data rights and warranties. Support in the updating of legal playbooks to reflect shifting industry standards with the Commercial Legal Team.
Legal Research & Diligence: Support in and conduct factual and legal research, organize complex documentation for technology partnerships, M&A diligence, and legal disputes in a distributed environment.
Trade Compliance Support: Develop a foundational understanding of Elastic's product and its technical intricacies to provide backup support to our core trade compliance team. Learn to analyze and help apply export laws, such as the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), specifically as they relate to our product capabilities and software portfolio.

Experience: 2–5+ years of experience in patent prosecution and/or litigation and intellectual property or product law, preferably with exposure to the software industry. SaaS, enterprise data platforms, or open-source products.
Technical Background: A bachelor's or advanced degree in a science or engineering field. Experience in or academic background in software engineering is a strong plus.
Credentials: Admission to the US or Canadian Patent Bar (registration number required). A JD from a US law school or LLB from a Canadian law school preferred, but patent agents are eligible.
Patent Proficiency: Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, or managing patent applications, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear patent claims and legal analysis.
Technical Curiosity: A demonstrated interest in Generative Artificial Intelligence and the legal frameworks governing code and data.
Problem-Solving: A self-starting, proactive approach with the poise to prioritize multiple projects and recalibrate advice as priorities shift.
Communication: Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to take complex legal and technical concepts and simplify the issues and desired outcomes.
Aptitude for Trade Compliance: A strong curiosity and willingness to learn trade compliance frameworks and analyze export law in relation to technical product details; prior trade compliance experience is not required.

Process Perspective: A desire to build and strengthen workflows and "productization" processes that help a legal team scale.
Global Perspective: Comfortable working across time zones and cultures in a distributed culture with a flexible approach to problem-solving.

Figuring out what’s “best for the company” always begins with thinking about what’s “best for players.” Every policy or contract that we draft; every lawsuit that we file or defend against; every letter we send; and all the legal advice that we give to our business partners, must always be done with our players’ interests in mind.

We are looking for a Counsel who thrives in a dynamic, collaborative environment to support our growing intellectual property needs. Interpreting the FOIA as it applies to the disclosure or withholding of NLRB records to advise the Branch staff and furnishes advice and interpretation to the Agency's offices including the Regional Offices and the Office of Congressional and Public Affairs regarding Agency FOIA policy in order to facilitate responses to inquiries from Congress, the press, or the general public.

Communicating with Regional offices and other Branches of the Agency to ensure that the FOIA Branch's responses to FOIA requests will not interfere with the operations of the Agency and the enforcement of the National Labor Relations Act.

About the Office The United States Trustee Program (USTP or Program) is a litigating component of the Department of Justice whose mission is to promote the integrity and efficiency of the bankruptcy system for the benefit of all stakeholders, including debtors, creditors, and the public.

The Program operates nationwide through twenty-one (21) regions comprised of 82 field office locations and exercises broad administrative, regulatory, and enforcement authority in bankruptcy cases.

Its responsibilities extend across chapter 7 and 13 consumer matters, chapter 12 family farmer cases, small business reorganizations, and complex chapter 11 corporate restructurings.

As the only participant in the bankruptcy process with a national footprint and independent oversight mandate, the USTP is uniquely positioned to identify and address multijurisdictional misconduct and other issues of national significance that threaten the integrity of the bankruptcy system.

At the same time, the Program remains equipped to respond effectively to local matters involving fraud, abuse, or other practices undermining the fair and efficient administration of bankruptcy cases. Job Description The U.S.

Trustee Program (USTP) is seeking an attorney with experience in litigation and bankruptcy law to oversee bankruptcy cases filed in the federal judicial districts served by the Region and/or field office.

Responsibilities include litigating enforcement matters on behalf of the Program, supervising private trustees, handling appellate matters, and referring potential criminal conduct identified through bankruptcy oversight.

The Program aims to hire skilled Trial Attorneys and provide them with frequent, meaningful courtroom experience across a wide range of issues arising in bankruptcy cases. Typical duties of a field office Trial Attorney include: Overseeing the administration of bankruptcy cases filed in the judicial districts served by the Region and field office.

Litigating issues arising in chapter 11 cases, including matters related to corporate governance, employment applications, fee applications, disclosure statements, and plan confirmation.

Litigating civil enforcement matters in consumer bankruptcy cases, including discharge objections, dismissal proceedings involving debtors' ability to repay creditors, attorney misconduct, and misconduct by non-attorney document preparation services. Assisting with appellate matters arising in the Region and District.

Partnering with the Executive Office and the United States Trustee on issues of national importance to support the Program's mission locally and to help develop and implement policies that ensure uniform application of bankruptcy law.

Supervising private trustees who administer cases filed under chapters 7, 13, 11, Subchapter V, and 12 of the Bankruptcy Code. Collaborating with Program bankruptcy Auditors, Paralegal Specialists, and other support staff in the Region.

Working with federal and state law enforcement partners to report criminal activity identified through bankruptcy case oversight. Conducting outreach to stakeholders in the bankruptcy system, including the bankruptcy court, bar, and other federal and state agencies. Participating in national projects and priorities, as assigned.

There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people.

Sub-Competencies: Knowledge of the American System of Government: Demonstrates understanding and appreciation of the American system of government, including the Constitution, the Bill of Rights, separation of powers, federalism, and the historical development of the American Nation.

Commitment to the Rule of Law: Upholds the principles of the American Founding, including equality under the law and democratic self-government. Ensures the law is applied fairly and consistently.

Civic-Mindedness: Stays up-to-date on important developments in American government and aligns organizational objectives and practices with presidential and public interests. Demonstrates a commitment to serve the American people.

ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades.

Sub-Competencies: Fiscal Responsibility: Strategically manages, allocates and monitors financial resources. Aligns priorities and initiatives to justify budget proposals. Monitors expenditures, cuts unnecessary costs, and uses cost-benefit analysis to set priorities.

Managing Resources: Manages resources efficiently and effectively based on current and projected organizational goals, skills, budget considerations, and staffing needs. Leveraging Technology: Explores emerging technology and potential applications. Incorporates technology to enhance efficiency and achieve results.

Ensures access to and security of technology systems. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality.

Sub-Competencies: Technical Skill: Possesses the requisite technical knowledge and subject matter expertise to consistently produce timely, high-quality work. Is considered a strong contributor in his or her domain. Problem Solving: Engages in critical and data-driven thinking when diagnosing root causes and evaluating options.

Identifies and promptly addresses the most pressing, high-priority problems. Agility and Resilience: Anticipates and adapts to change, new ideas, new information, and new conditions. Is committed to continuous improvement. Deals effectively with pressure and remains optimistic and persistent, even under adversity.

ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable.

Sub-Competencies: Accountability: Ensures that employees are appropriately recruited, selected, appraised, trained, and retained. Takes swift action to address performance- or conduct-based deficiencies in employees supervised. Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results.

Developing Others: Recognizes and rewards outstanding achievement in others. Develops the ability of others to perform and contribute to the organization by providing opportunities to learn through formal and informal methods. Cultivates a dynamic environment in which employees are not afraid to make mistakes.

Executive Judgement: Makes well-reasoned, timely, and effective decisions and considers short- and long-term implications. Communicates effectively with stakeholders across all organizational levels, sharing and guarding information where appropriate.

ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Sub-Competencies: Operational Mindset: Effectively translates strategies into actionable steps and processes.

Partners effectively with stakeholders to drive adoption and addresses blockers to ensure successful implementation. Innovation: Applies creativity to improving products and processes, challenges convention, takes measured risks, and considers ways to simplify and remove unnecessary requirements.

Strategic Thinking: Formulates objectives and priorities and implements plans consistent with the long-term interests of the organization by evaluating conditions, resources, capabilities, constraints, and organizational goals and values.

Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

See "Required Documents" section for additional information.

About the Office By delegation from the Attorney General, the Assistant Attorney General in charge of the Office of Legal Counsel (OLC) provides legal advice to the President and all executive branch agencies.

The Office provides written opinions and other advice in response to requests from the Attorney General, the Counsel to the President, the General Counsels of the various agencies of the Executive Branch, and other components of the Department of Justice.

Such requests typically deal with legal issues of particular complexity and importance or those about which two or more agencies disagree. The Office is also responsible for reviewing and commenting on the constitutionality of pending legislation.

All executive orders and substantive proclamations proposed to be issued by the President are reviewed by OLC for form and legality, as are various other matters that require the President's formal approval. The Office reviews all proposed orders of the Attorney General including regulations that require the Attorney General's approval.

It also performs a variety of special assignments referred by the Attorney General or the Deputy Attorney General. Job Description The Office of Legal Counsel, U.S. Department of Justice, is seeking highly qualified attorneys to serve as Attorney-Advisers in Washington, D.C.

The Office's principal function is to assist the Attorney General in fulfilling the role of legal adviser to the President and Executive Branch agencies. For more information, please visit OLC's internet website, http://www.usdoj.gov/olc/.

OLC's responsibilities include the following: Advising the Attorney General, the Counsel to the President, the General Counsels of executive departments and agencies, and the various components of the Department of Justice on constitutional and statutory matters; Resolving legal disputes within the Executive Branch through the issuance of authoritative legal opinions; Reviewing for constitutionality proposed legislation; and Reviewing for form and legality all executive orders and substantive proclamations and memoranda proposed to be issued by the President as well as all Attorney General Orders including regulations that require the Attorney General's approval.
Applicants must have a J.D. degree, be an active member of the bar (any jurisdiction) and have at least one year of post-J.D. legal experience. OLC is highly selective in its hiring because OLC attorneys handle some of the most difficult and important legal issues confronting the Executive Branch.

The ideal candidate would have exceptional academic credentials, a judicial clerkship or comparable experience, a strong background in constitutional law, outstanding legal research and writing skills, and the ability to obtain a Top-Secret security clearance.

Each division investigates and challenges anticompetitive conduct, mergers, and acquisitions in a wide range of industries, including: Mergers I: pharmaceuticals, medical devices, consumer health products, defense, aviation, and technology sectors.

Mergers II: semiconductors and other high-tech hardware; industrial chemicals, mining, commercial software, music, and video games. Mergers III: energy-related industries including crude oil and natural gas, retail gas stations, terminals, and pipelines, as well as online real estate and mortage origination systems, and consumer products.

Mergers IV: health care providers, office supply distribution, food distribution, casino services, supermarkets, specialty retail stores, and consumer goods. Anticompetitive Practices I: investigates potentially anticompetitive conduct in industries other than health care and pharmaceuticals.

Health Care: price-fixing, group boycotts, exclusive dealing, monopolization, and mergers-involving physicians and other health professionals, pharmaceutical companies, hospitals, and other institutional providers.

**Contract Manager (80-100%) \_ CDD 3 mois minimum**
La FHVi est un acteur clé dans le soutien métier, organisationnel et numérique des établissements sanitaires - hôpitaux, pharmacies d-hôpitaux, réseaux de soins, EMS et centres de secours et d-urgences - en Suisse romande. L'association reconnue d'utilité publique, à but non lucratif se trouve à Prilly sur le site de l'hôpital de Cery.
Elle s'engage à soutenir les établissements de santé grâce à son expertise en technologies de l'information et en gestion sanitaire. Son rôle est d-améliorer l'efficacité, la coordination et l'infrastructure numérique à travers des solutions adaptées à une clientèle diversifiée, tant par la taille des structures que par les métiers concernés.

En s'appuyant sur un système d'information mutualisé et des services numériques de qualité, elle vise à garantir une organisation hospitalière sûre et performante, centrée sur les besoins de la patientèle.
Face à la digitalisation croissante du système de santé, la FHVi a récemment entamé sa propre transformation pour répondre efficacement aux enjeux de ce domaine à la fois complexe, dynamique et passionnant. Cette transformation implique, entre autres, une refonte en profondeur du modèle de financement. Cela comprend une amélioration significative de la gestion budgétaire ainsi que la mise en place de pratiques financières plus robustes et transparentes.
Dans ce contexte, l-organisation recherche un.e

Rattaché·e au directeur administratif et financier, à la croisée des domaines juridique, financier et opérationnel, vous optimiserez le programme d-achats de la DSI et serez le·la garant·e de la fiabilité des contrats et aiderez les différents départements à atteindre leurs objectifs.

* Définit et garantit l-application rigoureuse d-un processus d-achat cohérant, tant pour les achats standards que pour ceux soumis à la réglementation des marchés publics (appel d-offre et appel d-offre public), en conformité avec les seuils, procédures en vigueur et le Règlement des signatures.
* Conçoit et met en œuvre, en collaboration avec les équipes opérationnelles, les consultations (RFI, RFP, RFQ).
* Assure le sourcing et l-identification des prestataires pertinents et prépare, coordonne et anime les phases de consultation et de soutenance des candidats.
* Élabore des grilles d-analyse multicritères et évalue les offres sur les plans technique, fonctionnel et commercial.
* Conduit les négociations, qu-elles soient en gré à gré ou dans le cadre formalisé des consultations, en étroite coordination avec les expert·es techniques (DSI, directions métiers) et les juristes.
* Contribue activement au processus de sélection des fournisseurs et à la formalisation contractuelle des accords.

* Suivi et animation des relations avec les fournisseurs stratégiques, analyse des reportings, revue des contrats et des dépenses, organisation et pilotage des comités de suivi.
* Définition et mise en œuvre d'une stratégie d-optimisation de la performance des contrats tout au long de leur cycle de vie.
* Analyse des dépenses : collecte, consolidation et analyse des données achats par fournisseur et par catégorie ; élaboration de synthèses et recommandations.
* Suivi de la performance achats : production et suivi des indicateurs clés (KPI), reporting régulier et présentation des résultats au management.
* Gestion des contrats clés : veille active sur les échéances, les engagements contractuels et les risques associés ; alerte et recommandations à destination de la direction.
* Participation ou pilotage d-analyses de risques fournisseurs et marché, intégrées aux processus décisionnels.
* Veille stratégique : surveillance continue des évolutions du marché, des innovations technologiques et des évolutions réglementaires impactant les achats.
* Réalisation d-analyses comparatives pour identifier les meilleures pratiques et opportunités d-optimisation.
**Profil recherché**
Doté·e d-une personnalité ouverte, bienveillante et orientée solutions, vous justifiez d-une solide expérience dans une société de services, idéalement en environnement IT, et manifestez un intérêt marqué pour les enjeux technologiques et contractuels.
Votre excellente maîtrise des leviers financiers, alliée à une aisance naturelle avec les chiffres, vous permet de piloter efficacement la performance contractuelle tout au long du cycle de vie des contrats. Vous savez interpréter des données complexes, identifier les risques, et recommander des actions correctives pertinentes.
Communicant·e hors pair, vous interagissez avec fluidité au sein d-équipes transversales, tout en assurant un lien constant avec les parties prenantes internes et externes. Vous êtes à l-aise dans la négociation, l-animation de comités de suivi, et la coordination avec les services juridiques, achats, finance ou opérationnels.
**Un temps partiel peut être envisagé entre 80 et 100%.**
**Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?**
Une association en pleine croissance, orientée vers l-innovation et la qualité de service. Une ambiance de travail collaborative et bienveillante, où l-initiative est valorisée. L-opportunité de contribuer directement à la performance et à la stratégie de l-association.
Notre association étant sensible aux questions de diversité et de mixité, nous encourageons les postulations féminines.

**Am Puls der Wirtschaft!** Da bewegen wir uns im Handelsregisteramt Kanton Zürich und bearbeiten mit unseren rund 80 Mitarbeitenden jedes Jahr über 70'000 Geschäftsfälle. Wir sind die zentrale Anlaufstelle für alle Unternehmenseintragungen im Kanton Zürich und tragen damit entscheidend zu Transparenz und Rechtssicherheit im Wirtschaftsverkehr bei.
Möchtest du eine bedeutende Fachabteilung (kaufmännische Mitarbeitende, Paralegal sowie Juristinnen und Juristen) führen und gleichzeitig die Zukunft unseres Amtes mitgestalten? Verbindest du juristische Fachkompetenz mit moderner Führung, digitalem Denken und einem klaren Blick für das Ganze? Dann freuen wir uns, dich kennenzulernen!
Als unsere neue **Leiterin oder unser neuer Leiter der Abteilung Sachbearbeitung** führst du rund 45 Mitarbeitende in vier Teams über die Teamleitenden. Du startest per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung.
### Diese Aufgaben warten auf Dich ###
* Du führst die Abteilung Sachbearbeitung fachlich und personell und entwickelst deine Teamleitenden sowie Mitarbeitenden gezielt weiter.
* Du gibst Orientierung, vereinbarst klare Ziele und sorgst dafür, dass die Abteilung ihre qualitativen und quantitativen Vorgaben erreicht.
* Du sorgst für eine einheitliche Praxis, eine hohe Arbeitsqualität sowie effiziente und kundenfreundliche Eintragungsverfahren.
* Du entscheidest komplexe oder umstrittene Handelsregistergeschäfte, verfasst Stellungnahmen in Beschwerdeverfahren und wirkst bei Vernehmlassungen mit.
* Du förderst den fachlichen Austausch und stärkst die Zusammenarbeit über Abteilungsgrenzen hinweg.
* Als Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung gestaltest du Strategien, Projekte und die Weiterentwicklung des Amtes aktiv mit. Du informierst frühzeitig über den Geschäftsgang, erkennst Risiken und bringst tragfähige Lösungen ein.
* In deiner Funktion als stellvertretende Amtsleitung übernimmst du bei Abwesenheit der Amtsleitung die Gesamtverantwortung und triffst die notwendigen Entscheide.
### Was bringst du mit? ###
* Du hast ein Masterstudium in Rechtswissenschaften oder eine gleichwertige juristische Ausbildung abgeschlossen.
* Du verfügst über langjährige Berufserfahrung, davon mehrere Jahre in einem juristischen Fachgebiet und mindestens drei Jahre in einer anspruchsvollen Führungsfunktion.
* Du kennst dich im Gesellschaftsrecht, Handelsregisterrecht oder in einem vergleichbaren Rechtsgebiet fundiert aus und bewegst dich sicher in komplexen Verwaltungsverfahren.
* Du hast Erfahrung darin, eine grössere Organisationseinheit über Führungspersonen zu leiten, und verbindest Vertrauen und Freiraum mit klaren Erwartungen.
* Du denkst strategisch und konzeptionell, bleibst gleichzeitig nahe am operativen Geschäft und setzt Entscheide konsequent um.
* Du treibst Veränderungen aktiv voran, hinterfragst bestehende Abläufe und nutzt digitale Technologien sowie neue Arbeitsformen mit Freude und Neugier.
* Du kommunizierst klar, verbindlich und adressatengerecht. Unterschiedliche Meinungen siehst du als Chance für bessere Lösungen.
* Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse. Englisch- und Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.
### Du darfst einiges erwarten ###
Dich erwartet eine verantwortungsvolle Schlüsselposition mit grossem Gestaltungsspielraum und direktem Einfluss auf die Weiterentwicklung des Handelsregisteramtes. Obwohl wir uns in einem engen gesetzlichen Rahmen bewegen, denken wir nicht in starren Mustern. Wir sind digital fortschrittlich, verbessern unsere Arbeitsweise laufend und pflegen eine offene, unkomplizierte Zusammenarbeit. Anspruchsvolle Themen, klare Entscheide und eine gute Portion Humor haben bei uns gleichermassen Platz.
Unsere Büros liegen zentral in Zürich. Zudem bietet dir der Kanton Zürich fortschrittliche Anstellungsbedingungen und vielfältige Möglichkeiten, dich fachlich und persönlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Sie sind die zentrale Anlaufstelle für rechtliche, steuerliche und regulatorische Fragen im Geschäftsbereich Vermögensanlagen (GBA).

Sie beurteilen Investitionsformen und \-vehikel aus rechtlicher Sicht und hinterfragen rechtliche Due\-Diligence\-Prüfungen externer Partner.
Sie verantworten den Fachbereich Steuern im GBA: Sie verfolgen relevante Entwicklungen, plausibilisieren steuerliche Abklärungen und Due\-Diligence\-Arbeiten externer Spezialisten und stellen gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern eine sachgerechte und steuerlich effiziente Umsetzung der Investitionen sicher.

Sie leiten die Fachgruppe Datenschutz und bringen juristische Expertise in bereichsübergreifende Projekte und Fragestellungen der PKZH ein.

Sie verfügen über ein abgeschlossenes juristisches Hochschulstudium (Master of Law / lic. iur. oder gleichwertig) ergänzt mit einem Anwaltspatent.

Sie können steuerliche Fragestellungen im Zusammenhang mit Kapitalanlagen fundiert einordnen und Arbeiten externer Steuerexperten kritisch plausibilisieren.

Join the Sleep Fitness Movement
At Eight Sleep, we’re on a mission to fuel human potential through optimal sleep. As the world’s first sleep fitness company, we’re redefining what it means to be well-rested and building the most advanced hardware, software, and AI technology to make it possible. Our products power peak mental, physical, and emotional performance by transforming every night of sleep into a personalized, data-driven recovery experience.
Every role at Eight Sleep is a chance to create cutting-edge technology, collaborate with world-class talent, and help shape a future where sleep isn’t passive — it’s a powerful tool for living better. If you’re tired of the ordinary and driven to build at the edge of what’s possible, this is your moment. Join us and lead the movement that’s transforming how the world sleeps and what we’re all capable of when we wake up.
High Standards. No Apologies.
We operate with intensity because our mission demands it. At Eight Sleep, we bring the same mindset as the world’s top performers: focused, relentless, and always pushing to be in the top 1% of our craft. This isn’t a 9-to-5. Our team is deeply committed, often putting in the extra effort — not because we’re told to, but because we’re invested in building something category-defining.

Eight Sleep’s legal team is one person today: our first in-house legal counsel, who handles everything from IP and litigation to privacy, regulatory, and commercial matters. You’d be the second lawyer, reporting to her, and for a while the team is the two of you.
Your home-base is privacy and regulatory, and there’s a lot of it: the privacy program, FTC and consumer protection, advertising and subscription compliance, product and market-entry questions, and the healthcare-regulatory work that comes with our newer product lines. But this isn’t a role for someone who only wants to live in that lane.

What matters most is that you’re willing to take on whatever lands on the department, and that you’re a genuine generalist, just as comfortable picking up a commercial contract, a litigation question, or a product counseling call when that’s what the week calls for.
This is a build role. The company has grown quickly and the legal function is still taking shape, so you’ll be creating programs and processes rather than inheriting them, with a lot of room to own your work. It’s a good fit for someone who’s a self-starter, works hard, and is comfortable making decisions on their own without a lot of process.

Privacy and data protection
Build and run our global privacy program across the frameworks that apply to us (CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, and others): disclosures, consent, records of processing, and data subject requests.
Own data processing agreements across our vendors, cross-border transfer and localization compliance, and our breach response playbook.
Handle compliance for the biometric and health data at the center of our product, and run privacy reviews for new features, integrations, and AI models.
Regulatory and consumer protection
Own FTC and consumer protection: health and wellness claims, advertising review, and subscription and auto-renewal compliance across our markets.
Keep a practical read on what each market requires (product registration, import, labeling, disclosures) so we clear the way before we launch somewhere new.
Track medical device and healthcare-regulatory questions as our health features grow, and help scope the legal path for new product categories (FDA classification, corporate practice of medicine, anti-kickback, HIPAA).
Beyond privacy and regulatory (this part matters here)
Take on whatever the department needs outside your core area: commercial contracts, litigation support, product counseling, and the rest of the in-house docket.
Act as embedded counsel to product and engineering, and help build out the function and legal operations alongside our in-house counsel.

JD and active bar membership in at least one US state.
8 to 12 years of relevant experience, including meaningful time in-house. This role moves quickly, and we’re not looking for someone coming straight from private practice.
Solid working knowledge of the privacy and regulatory areas that matter to us: US privacy (CCPA/CPRA), GDPR, and FTC and consumer protection.
Above all, a versatile generalist. You’ve worked across more than one area in-house, and you’re comfortable picking up an unfamiliar matter and figuring it out.
A self-starter who works hard, makes decisions independently, and advises the business directly rather than routing everything to outside counsel.
Comfortable in a fast-moving environment where you build rather than maintain.

In-house experience at a consumer technology, healthtech, wearable, or DTC subscription company.
Experience as a first or early regulatory or privacy hire.
Biometric or health data experience, and cross-border transfer or data localization experience.
Advertising, health-claims, or healthcare-regulatory experience (HIPAA, corporate practice of medicine, the FDA/FTC intersection).
Familiarity with AI governance and emerging AI regulation.
CIPP/US or CIPP/E is a plus, not a requirement; we weight experience over credentials.

We're looking for an interim In-house Legal Counsel to join our Legal team at Pleo in Copenhagen, Denmark. In this role, you'll serve as a trusted legal advisor across the business, protecting our interests and enabling growth as we scale our fintech platform. If you're excited about working at the intersection of legal strategy and operational excellence, and are passionate about building a compliant, well-governed fintech company, then this is the opportunity for you!
Please note that the role is a parental leave cover and therefore fixed-term until 30 September 2027.
Who you’ll be working with and reporting to
You'll report to one of our Associate Director, Legal and work closely with teams in People, Fraud, Finance, Product, Compliance and Operations. Our legal team is highly collaborative and dedicated to managing legal risk while enabling business velocity.
What you’ll be doing

s.h: As an In-house Legal Counsel, you will
s.t:
Serve as the primary point of contact for business queries across all departments, providing timely, practical legal guidance on day-to-day operational matters.
Support our People team on employment law, workplace policies, and labor compliance, including contract reviews, policy drafting, and regulatory adherence across multiple jurisdictions.
Corporate administration by drafting, reviewing, and amending internal policies, procedures, and standardised legal templates that the business can use efficiently.
Assist managing fraud and compliance escalations by conducting liability assessments, performing compliance checks, and providing risk mitigation advice to protect the business.
Assist with customer disputes and regulatory engagement with the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS), supporting escalations, preparing responses, and helping to ensure we meet all regulatory deadlines and requirements.

s.h: You'll thrive in this role if you have
s.t:
A Cand.Jur or equivalent legal qualification recognised in Denmark.
2-5 years of legal experience – ideally in fintech, financial services, or a fast-growing scale-up environment where you've handled a broad range of matters.
Knowledge about employment law and HR compliance – you understand the nuances of employment contracts, workplace policies, and labor law across multiple jurisdictions.
Strong vendor and contract management skills – you can review, negotiate, and draft commercial agreements efficiently.
Excellent communication skills – you can translate complex legal concepts into practical business advice for non-legal stakeholders.
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset – you see problems as opportunities and can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Experience with compliance and risk management in a regulated industry is a plus as well as managing regulatory escalations and disputes, particularly with financial regulators or ombudsman services.
Why is this role a good fit for you

s.h: This role is a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want a real look at how the law works in practice, where you implement it and explain it rather than argue it in theory
You want genuine input into decisions, balancing the technically correct answer against what actually works commercially
You like building things that outlast you: templates, policies and process that the business will use long after your contract ends

s.h: This role is not a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want a clean roadmap. The team is under-resourced and the workload is heavy, so expect more firefighting than planned work
You're looking for a permanent role. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract covering parental leave
You want to specialise deeply or lead. This is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role where you'll be supported, not managing
How you’ll develop in this role

s.h: In your first three months at Pleo, you'll
s.t:
Take over the routine employment workload so it runs independently of your manager
Get to know the business well enough that your advice fits how Pleo actually operates, not just what the regulation says
Start shaping the policies and templates the move from startup to corporate needs
Across the 12 months you'll build in-house practice and a working knowledge of fintech regulation that's hard to get anywhere else, with direct support from an experienced lead. Plenty of people use a contract like this as the step that takes them from theory into commercial legal work for good.
The location
This role will is a hybrid role with an expectation of spending on average 3 days a week in our Copenhagen office.

💳 Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
🍜 Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
🏥 Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

🏖️ Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

Intro call (30 minutes) – A chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role, your background, and what's important to you in your next move.
Interview with our Associate Director, Legal (45 minutes) – Meet to discuss how you see your role supporting the business, your approach to compliance culture, and your vision for the legal function.

Traditional banking has never really given you control over your financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance .

What you'll be doing
As our Legal Counsel, you'll provide high-level legal guidance within the Fintech sector, particularly in payments, e-money, and consumer credit products, offering strategic counsel on regulatory, contractual, and product-related matters to ensure compliance and mitigate risks.

s.h: Here's what that looks like in practice
s.t:
Product development support – Collaborate cross-functionally to design and launch new products and services in Payments and Consumer Credit (such as BNPL), integrating basic technical and engineering considerations into legal analysis.
Risk assessment & management – Identify legal and regulatory risks, proposing effective mitigation strategies aligned with our risk appetite to safeguard the organisation.
Regulatory compliance – Advise on relevant financial regulatory requirements, including PSD2, AML/KYC, e-money regulations, and CCD2, ensuring adherence.
Stakeholder management – Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, providing pragmatic legal guidance and fostering a culture of legal awareness across the organisation.

This role needs someone strategic, analytically strong, and equipped with deep fintech and payments regulatory knowledge to navigate complex legal frameworks.
Relevant education – Qualified lawyer with a minimum of 5 years PQE, and ideally 8–10 years of professional legal experience.
Relevant technical and regulatory knowledge – Deep knowledge of financial and consumer credit regulations (PSD2, AML/KYC, EMRs, CCD2) and a demonstrable track record in Fintech and Payments, ideally with experience in both private practice and in-house settings.
Analytical mindset – Ability to dive deep into complex legal issues, exercise strong judgment, and make sound risk-based decisions.

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.
We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.
Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor . Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps.

Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

We're hiring a Senior Privacy Counsel to be a core member of Sierra's growing legal team. This role will report to our Associate General Counsel, Product and Privacy, as part of our growing privacy legal function.

We are looking for someone who has deep expertise in privacy counseling, AI privacy regulation, and commercial privacy support (e.g., DPAs, BAAs, and MSA privacy provisions). You will thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy tackling challenges beyond your comfort zone, and be excited to contribute across the business.

In return, we'll provide the support and opportunities you need to grow and excel as a lawyer. You'll be part of a legal team that is highly respected within the company — committed to excellence, collaboration, and making a meaningful impact.
Privacy
Advise product, engineering, operations, marketing and other cross-functional teams on compliance with global privacy laws and related regulation applicable to Sierra’s business, including GDPR, the EU AI Act, DORA, etc.
Build and own Sierra’s privacy counseling and compliance program as we scale globally.
Develop specific privacy regulation expertise in core regulated industries of Sierra customers, such as healthcare, insurance, banking, telecommunications, and financial services.
Support the commercial legal team and GTM teams by drafting, reviewing, and negotiating the commercial privacy aspects of transactional work, including data processing agreements, business associate agreements, and other privacy-related transactional documents.

Develop training materials and conduct training sessions for product and business teams.
Regulatory (with focus on AI)
Advise on all aspects of emerging AI-specific privacy regulations and their applicability to Sierra’s business.
Develop and implement AI governance policies and frameworks to ensure responsible AI deployment, ethical data usage, and regulatory adherence.
Monitor and interpret global AI and privacy regulations, advising leadership on risks, trends, and strategic compliance initiatives.
Represent Sierra in discussions with regulators, industry groups, and external stakeholders on privacy and AI governance matters.

8+ years of legal experience, with a combination of large international law firm and in-house experience at a tech company.
Deep knowledge of global privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, and other US state privacy laws) and AI regulatory frameworks (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework).
A passion for AI, with a deep understanding of AI products, LLMs and the related legal issues, and personal experience with integrating AI into your work.
Experience mentoring and managing more junior team members.

Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to partner with both legal and non-legal stakeholders.
A strong work ethic with an eye for detail. You will strive for perfection, and expect that of others.

Even better…
Experience building a privacy program in a regulated industry (healthcare, financial services, insurance, banking, telecommunications), and/or at a high-growth technology company.
Experience engaging with regulators and policymakers on AI and privacy issues.
CIPP/US, CIPP/E, or similar certification.
Previous experience developing trust and safety or responsible AI programs.
Startup experience and comfort with rapid iteration and ambiguity.

Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.
Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.
Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.
Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.
Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

Curious, reliable, comfortable moving uncomfortably fast, and - above all else - have a low ego.

We are looking for a Senior AI Governance Counsel to join our Global DPO Office and help build, roll out, and operate Adyen's enterprise AI governance framework.

Sitting within the group that owns our global privacy program and AI governance, and supports incident response and management as well as data governance, you will be the driving force in shaping our strong foundations into a consistent, enterprise-wide AI governance program that scales with Adyen's ambitions - helping the business innovate boldly and responsibly with AI.

You will translate the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, GDPR, the CCPA/CPRA, and emerging global AI and privacy requirements into pragmatic policies, standards, and assessment workflows - and partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory and Engineering to make them real.

Help build, roll out, and embed Adyen's enterprise-wide AI governance framework, policies, and standards, driving consistency as AI adoption scales across the business.
Design and operationalize AI risk and impact assessments across the AI lifecycle - from intake and risk classification through deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning - with particular focus on generative and agentic AI use cases.
Interpret the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and other applicable AI laws across Adyen's global footprint, and translate them into practical policies, playbooks, and procedures for first-line teams.
Support the teams that maintain Adyen's AI inventories by defining governance parameters and requirements for cataloguing and risk-classifying AI tools and use cases.
Develop enterprise guidance and a consistent approach for evaluating AI systems, covering performance, fairness, and explainability expectations appropriate to each use case's risk profile.
Design simple, proportionate, risk-tiered processes and “green paths” that make responsible AI the easy path for fast-moving teams - using clear risk tiers and practical incentives so the compliant route is also the most convenient one.
Translate model-evaluation techniques - including fairness, bias, and adversarial (red-teaming) testing - into clear procedures that technology teams can apply to their own models and tools.
Partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory, and Engineering to run the AI governance program and align on controls, escalation, and human-oversight protocols.
Advise on privacy considerations across the AI lifecycle, coordinating with the wider DPO Office on the interaction between AI assessments and data protection.
Design and deliver AI governance training and promote AI literacy and a culture of responsible, accountable AI use.
Monitor global AI and privacy developments and translate them into proportionate governance requirements, supporting responses to audit, regulatory, and client inquiries.

7+ Years in AI Governance/Privacy: Proven background building, deploying, and managing global AI or privacy governance programs, ideally within regulated, multi-jurisdictional environments.
Legal / Risk Qualification: Qualified lawyer or governance professional with substantial experience in AI governance, privacy, or technology risk. (US jurisdiction admission is a plus).

Anticipate and identify data protection obligations and risks, and help address them in a practical, scalable, and privacy-by-design manner.

Engage with regional stakeholders and, where appropriate, local regulators and external counsel, building trusted relationships that strengthen Adyen's regional privacy capability.

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Anthropic is seeking a Regulatory Counsel to lead our legal work on AI regulation in the United States and to support our global AI regulatory posture.

This is a senior in-house legal role for a commercially driven lawyer ready to take commercial legal programs work with partners and negotiate technology deals. The role reports directly to the Head of Commercial Legal, Strategic Growth.
We operate a hybrid go-to-market model that combines demand-led direct sales, solution-led growth, and indirect distribution through a tiered partner and channel ecosystem. We reach organizations globally through technology alliances, GSI relationships, channel partners, and reseller arrangements — powering learning and capability-building at scale. Legal sits at the center of all three motions.
You will be a dedicated legal partner for B2B Enterprise, Technology Alliances, and Channel and Distribution Partnerships, supporting the development and negotiation of the indirect partner ecosystem that underpins our scalable distribution. This is a role for someone who combines deep transactional expertise with strong business instincts, operates with a high degree of independence, and is ready to grow into broader leadership responsibility within a scaling legal function.

Exceptional business judgement and a proven ability to balance legal risk with commercial objectives in fast-moving deal environments.
Executive-level communication skills: able to distill complex issues into clear, actionable guidance and influence stakeholders from SMB to large enterprise and C-suite.
A track record of using approved AI tools to increase legal productivity, and staying current on AI governance obligations.
What you’ll be doing
B2B Enterprise, Ecosystems and Technology Transactions
Take primary ownership of drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial agreements across global system integrator arrangements, channel partner and reseller agreements, technology alliance and co-sell agreements, enterprise SaaS and platform licensing, API and technical integration agreements, and distribution and go-to-market partnerships.
Advise senior business stakeholders, including GTM leadership, and Product teams, on deal structuring, risk allocation, commercial terms, and multi-jurisdictional GTM considerations, serving as the day-to-day legal lead who positions Legal as a genuine business enabler.
Partner with the Product Legal team to develop and refine legal frameworks that support a self-serve and low-touch commercial motion, including API access agreements, developer terms, usage-based licensing structures, and SMB onboarding frameworks, contributing to a standardized, scalable approach that enables businesses to engage and onboard with speed and minimal friction.
Provide clear, solution-focused guidance on AI-related commercial arrangements, data-sharing agreements, and emerging technology implementations as they enter the enterprise deal mix.
Own and continuously develop the suite of enterprise and channel contracting templates, playbooks, negotiation guidelines, and approval frameworks used across the partnerships function.
Design scalable legal infrastructure that empowers fast-moving deal teams to execute efficiently while maintaining sound risk controls across both direct and indirect channels.
GTM Product Commercialisation and Third-Party Integration
Act as a primary legal partner for the commercialisation of GTM products, advising on go-to-market structures, route-to-market models, pricing and packaging frameworks, and the legal terms that govern how products are brought to market directly and through third parties.
Draft and negotiate agreements that govern the embedding, bundling, or distribution of our products within third-party platforms, marketplaces, and ecosystems, including white-label arrangements, OEM agreements, co-branded offerings, and platform integration terms.
Advise on licensing boundaries and revenue-sharing constructs as the product suite evolves and is commercialised through an expanding range of direct and indirect channels.
Work closely with Product, Product Legal, Marketing, and Sales to ensure commercial and legal structures keep pace with product development and new route-to-market initiatives, flagging and resolving legal considerations early in the product lifecycle.
What you’ll have
Genuinely commercial in your approach: able to identify and manage risk pragmatically, find workable solutions under pressure, and avoid being a blocker to growth.
An effective communicator and influencer, comfortable advising and challenging senior stakeholders across Sales, Product, and Executive leadership.
Qualified lawyer with 10+ years of post-qualification experience, including meaningful in-house tenure at a technology, SaaS, or enterprise software company.
A proven track record negotiating complex B2B technology agreements including GSI, channel, reseller, alliance, and enterprise platform deals, ideally within or alongside global organisations.
Demonstrable experience advising on product commercialisation, route-to-market strategy, or third-party distribution and embedding arrangements.
Comfortable operating across both high-touch enterprise deals and high-volume standardised indirect channel frameworks, understanding that each requires a different legal posture.
Highly organised and self-directed, with a demonstrated ability to manage a high-volume deal workload across competing priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision.
A collaborative team player who understands their place in a broader legal function and actively supports those around them, including upward to leadership
Posting Date: 15 September 2026
Application Window: 2 weeks
We anticipate the application window will be open until 30 September 2026. Based on business needs, this opportunity may remain posted beyond or closed before the anticipated application window.

Databricks seeks an experienced attorney with significant experience in international partner and channel programs to join our go-to-market legal team. This role will focus on program development across multiple jurisdictions. The ideal candidate is a proactive legal professional with substantial in-house experience in partner program development. This position offers a unique opportunity to influence the development of routes to market for groundbreaking technologies.
You will report to the VP, International General Counsel.
You have over 7 years of relevant legal experience, with a focus on partner and channel programs supporting complex technology transactions. You have meaningful experience negotiating commercial agreements and related knowledge of legal issues related to compliance, data privacy, information security, artificial intelligence, and intellectual property.

Transactions: Draft and negotiate partner agreements while managing legal engagements to align with regulatory and business needs; lead and/or assist in negotiations with strategic partners, balancing the expansive growth of our alliance network with long-term risk.
Program Management: Participate in the development / launch / evolution of new programs (solution offerings, partnering) by teaming with cross-functional business partners, client groups, and internal legal leads in a hyper-growth environment.
Channel & Technology: Support business development of channel distribution models and technology partnerships to build scalable processes to meet long-term growth objectives.
Compliance: Oversee compliance related to channel development and contracting in multiple jurisdictions, engaging closely with the Legal Compliance team.
Risk Assessment: Conduct compliance risk assessments in relevant jurisdictions and internal policy gap analyses; adjust Databricks’ channel programs as necessary.
Training & Education: Create and deliver training on ethics and compliance for stakeholders interfacing with channel partners.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with commercial counsel, operations, and other business units to ensure successful channel development to address Company goals for transacting at scale and rapid revenue growth; you will become a subject matter expert to your internal business partners, client groups, and colleagues, helping resolve challenges and seizing opportunities for success.

Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree from an accredited law school and admission to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.
8+ years of combined relevant legal experience at a law firm and within a high-growth technology company.
Proven ability to develop and implement effective partner programs across multiple jurisdictions.
Strong analytical skills with a demonstrated ability to convey complex legal concepts clearly and concisely.
Excellent interpersonal skills with a collaborative approach to working across teams.
A self-starter who is comfortable navigating ambiguous situations and providing sound legal judgment.
You have a programmatic mindset, experience managing multi-faceted projects, and an understanding of how to develop and simplify processes.
Requires deep experience in channel and partner model development, plus strong experience in contract drafting and negotiation in a high-tech industry context. It would be beneficial but not a requirement if you are familiar with ISV partnering, cloud marketplaces, and quote- to- cash principles. Prior experience developing and evolving contract templates would be a plus.
You are a critical thinker comfortable in speaking up and brainstorming productively, thinking of future needs/issues, while executing on current activities.
You apply a highly collaborative and positive approach to working with legal colleagues and business partners. You have a hands-on approach in executing, a builder mindset able to work independently but seeking and welcoming supportive input as appropriate.
You are experienced at making recommendations to senior leaders in a fast-paced environment and applying a practical, balanced mindset to legal problem-solving.

Experience working in multiple jurisdictions across EMEA, APJ, and LATAM.
Knowledge of platform technology and related contract models, including experience in drafting and negotiating high-value agreements, is a bonus.

About Doximity
Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity’s mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients.
At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you’re excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we’d love to hear from you.

We are hiring a Product Counsel, R&D / AI to serve as the primary legal partner to Doximity’s AI team. You will sit with the engineers, data scientists, and product managers building our clinical AI products — ambient documentation, clinical search and answers, and AI-powered clinician workflows — and help them ship quickly and responsibly. This is a hands-on, high-judgment role for a lawyer who wants to be in the room where AI products are designed, not downstream of them.

s.h: As a Product Counsel, R&D / AI, you will
s.t:
Act as embedded counsel to our AI and R&D teams, advising on product design, model development, and launch decisions from concept through release — and owning the most significant legal questions our AI organization faces.
Advise on health data throughout the AI lifecycle: HIPAA and HITECH, business associate arrangements, de-identification, permitted uses for model training and evaluation, and state health privacy and consent laws.
Counsel on AI-specific risk, including training data provenance and licensing, third-party model and API terms, output accuracy and reliability, clinical decision support and FDA software boundaries, intellectual property in AI outputs, and transparency and disclosure obligations.
Draft and negotiate the agreements R&D depends on — data licenses, model and infrastructure provider terms, research and clinical collaborations, BAAs and DPAs, and evaluation and pilot agreements.
Build the legal infrastructure that lets AI development scale: intake and review processes, product launch checklists, playbooks, self-service guidance, and training for engineering and product teams.
Partner closely with Privacy, Security, Regulatory, Clinical, Trust & Safety, and Marketing to align on governance for new AI capabilities.
Track the fast-moving AI and health data regulatory landscape and translate it into concrete, actionable product guidance.
Location: This role is In-Person in San Francisco, CA.

We’re excited to meet candidates who have many of the following qualifications:
J.D. and active membership in the California bar (or eligibility to register as in-house counsel in California).
California Bar membership preferred; alternatively, an attorney licensed in any U.S. jurisdiction and eligible to obtain RHIC may be considered.
Approximately 5–9 years of legal experience, including meaningful in-house time supporting a technology, digital health, or healthcare organization.
Demonstrated experience as product counsel — embedded with engineering and product teams, advising on features in flight rather than reviewing finished work.
Healthcare data fluency: HIPAA, business associate relationships, de-identification standards, and the practical realities of working with PHI. Digital health, health IT, or provider-facing experience strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of the legal issues specific to AI and machine learning — training data rights, model licensing, output liability, evaluation and monitoring, and emerging AI regulation.
Genuine hands-on facility with AI tools, and the technical curiosity to engage substantively with the people building models.
Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward practical, risk-calibrated advice delivered at product speed.
Clear, concise written communication and the ability to make legal complexity actionable for a technical audience.

About Faire
Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline.

At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores.

With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.
We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

Faire is hiring a Senior Counsel, Privacy & Product to help our teams build and ship a global wholesale marketplace that handles data thoughtfully. This role is ideal for a privacy expert who also loves to work directly with product teams and advise on a range of legal topics.

Reporting to the Deputy General Counsel, you will partner closely with our product and engineering teams, helping them craft practical solutions to navigate legal complexity.

You will also serve as Faire Legal’s in-house privacy and data expert and play a pivotal role in the development of Faire’s data governance program, advising on emerging privacy obligations and shaping the frameworks, processes, and playbooks that protect our data at scale.

Partner directly with Faire’s engineering, product, data, and design teams to provide practical legal guidance—across a wide range of legal domains—on product development and go-to-market strategy
Act as a senior legal advisor to the business on data governance issues, including privacy, data use, information security, retention and deletion, and cross-border data flows
Build and mature Faire’s data governance program, designing frameworks and processes, supporting implementation, and driving improvements as we learn what works
Track developments in global privacy laws and translate them into actionable guidance for the business
Draft and maintain privacy policies, notices, standards, playbooks, and training that scale good decision-making across the company

Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and an active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction
5+ years of legal experience at a law firm, in-house, or both, including substantive privacy work
Deep expertise in global privacy law, including EU and UK GDPR, CCPA and other state laws, and emerging frameworks
Experience counseling advertising product teams and/or online marketplaces is a plus
Experience with litigation or regulator engagement is a plus
Actively experimenting with AI in legal work, and excited to go deeper
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to provide risk-calibrated and solution-focused advice to product and engineering teams
Scrappy and resourceful – when something needs to get done, you find a way to make it happen
