At Flipdish, we’re turning the tables in favour of independent restaurant and takeaway owners by offering them powerful, simple-to-use tech solutions backed by real human support. Everything we do is designed to make running a restaurant satisfyingly simple in a world that’s anything but.

You’ll be part of the team supporting Flipdish’s mission to make running a restaurant satisfyingly simple. This role is a generalist role with an emphasis on two core regulatory mindset areas - employment law and data protection - alongside an interesting and varied mix of other legal work spanning corporate, M&A, IP and equity. .
You’ll partner closely with our People, Finance, Commercial, Product and Engineering teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to provide pragmatic, risk-aware guidance, help shape internal processes, and ensure the business stays compliant.
What you’ll own
Lead employment law support across the business
Lead data protection compliance key data-protection processes.
Steward privacy policy and marketing compliance : maintain privacy policy updates and ensure direct marketing practices (including SMS compliance) are handled lawfully.
Maintain training and standards for key teams (People, Support, and others) so compliance is practical and repeatable.
Challenge poor decisions and propose better ways of working. Constructive challenge is a responsibility - prioritising harmony over truth or progress is a failure of responsibility.
What success looks like
You are involved partner to the business who isn’t confined to their legal swim lane
You take a proactive approach to employment-law and handle issues consistently, with timely and well-documented advice.
You ensure data subject requests are handled with clear legal triage, governance, and defensible timelines.
You strengthen our compliance culture through targeted training and practical guidance that teams can apply.
You own Companies Act compliance for our Irish entities alongside third party company secretarial support.
You scan for relevant legal changes that will impact our business and take a proactive approach to getting ahead of these.
You are a key part of the team managing our employee equity structure.
You are well known in the Commercial team for transacting partner contracts and triaging some novel customer queries.

s.h: You’ll thrive in this role if you
s.t:
Have ~5+ years PQE (qualified as a solicitor in Ireland).
Can demonstrate strong experience across employment law and practical risk management.
Have credible GDPR / data protection experience, including comfort engaging with regulators and leading privacy assessments.
Communicate clearly with non-lawyers, translate legal risk into actionable next steps, and manage sensitive situations with discretion.
Take high ownership: you don’t wait to be told what to do.
Challenge poor decisions and propose better ways of working.
Embrace technology to augment your work and build efficient processes
The following would help you stand out.
In-house experience in a tech / data-driven environment.
Experience with privacy policy governance , marketing compliance, and operational DSAR oversight.
Exposure to other EU regulatory areas (e.g., digital or accessibility-related compliance) where privacy intersects.
What You Get
We’re a growing startup and we understand that amazing incentives will attract amazing talent. Alongside a competitive salary, we offer unparalleled opportunities for career growth. If you’re smart, ambitious, and hard-working, we’ll do whatever it takes to make you a Flipdisher!
Hub model (hybrid): a healthy blend of hub + home working (2 days per week from our Sandyford office)
Time off: 25 days annual leave + public holidays
Private healthcare
Pension: Retirement savings support (Ireland)
Equity (ESOP): share options, so you can share in Flipdish’s long-term success
Team connection: regular team meet-ups and company events
Commuter supports: TaxSaver / travel schemes (where available)

At Flipdish, we’re on the side of independent restaurant and takeaway owners, running busy operations on tight margins with rising costs, staffing challenges, and an increasingly demanding customer base. Our job is to make their lives easier with technology that’s powerful, satisfyingly simple, and backed by real human support.
Our integrated ecosystem, spanning online ordering, marketing, loyalty, point of sale, menu optimisation, and operational automation, helps restaurants grow while staying in control. We’re an AI-first company, and we use it to help our customers get better outcomes, faster ordering, smarter marketing, and smoother operations, so owners and teams can spend more time on what matters.
Inside the company, we value ownership and clarity, with a friendly, people-led culture behind it. We trust our people to help shape what kind of employer Flipdish is, not just follow a script. Grafana Labs is seeking a Senior Commercial Counsel to join our dedicated, collaborative, and fast-growing legal team. This role will serve as a strategic legal partner to the business, with primary responsibility for leading high-impact, revenue-generating transactions and supporting the Grafana Labs sales organization in structuring, negotiating, and closing complex enterprise on-premises and SaaS commercial agreements.
This role will also support broader legal matters, including reviewing and negotiating vendor and marketing agreements, advising on and supporting channel programs, contributing to privacy initiatives, maintaining commercial legal form agreements, and partnering on other cross-functional matters.
The successful candidate will be a creative and analytical thinker who is highly detail-oriented and embraces a business-oriented approach. They will have the ability to think strategically and build trusted advisor relationships with internal stakeholders.

The ideal candidate brings significant experience leading negotiations of complex, high-value commercial agreements with Fortune 500 and other sophisticated enterprise customers, often on customer paper and within highly regulated industries such as healthcare and financial services.
This individual is an exceptional drafter and strategic negotiator with strong business judgment, able to quickly distinguish between material legal risk and negotiable terms.

They take a pragmatic, solutions-oriented approach that balances legal protection with commercial objectives, ensuring negotiations remain constructive and deals continue progressing toward closure.

The candidate should have a proven track record as a trusted partner to sales, with demonstrated success managing sophisticated counterparties, navigating complex issues, and driving critical revenue-generating transactions through to timely and successful execution.

Lead strategy, negotiation, and execution of complex, high-value enterprise B2B agreements, including SaaS and on-premises licenses, data processing agreements (GDPR, CCPA), business associate agreements (HIPAA), information security agreements, professional services agreements, channel partner agreements, and other commercial and technology-related contracts.
Serve as a strategic partner to sales leadership on deal structuring, risk assessment, and negotiation strategy to accelerate revenue while protecting the business.
Partner with cross-functional teams (e.g., finance, security, support, product) to resolve complex commercial and operational issues and support new go-to-market models, pricing structures, and programs.
Develop and improve form agreements and negotiation playbooks to drive consistency and scalability.
Contribute to the development of workflows and processes that enable the legal team to scale effectively, including contract negotiation, execution, and tracking of contractual obligations.
Support global expansion efforts, including go-to-market initiatives, privacy-by-design, and security-by-design programs.
Create and deliver training to business teams on legal best practices, effective engagement with legal, and relevant legal and regulatory developments.

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:
As Associate General Counsel, Product & Regulatory, you'll own how legal and regulatory judgement shows up inside Mews' product and fintech work, leading a specialist pod of counsel and paralegals and reporting to the Chief Legal Officer.

Mews builds tightly integrated SaaS and fintech products, and the hard questions (money transmission, e-money, embedded finance, partner-bank and BaaS models, cross-border operating decisions) need someone who helps product teams work through them in practice, not from a distance.

This is a chance to set the bar for how a scaling hospitality-fintech platform builds regulated products responsibly and at pace.
You'll be embedded with Product and Engineering as a genuine product counsel and builder, surfacing and triaging legal and regulatory issues across the design and release lifecycle rather than reviewing work once it's done.

You'll own the Product & Regulatory legal remit end to end: setting priorities and the quality bar, deciding what the pod handles directly, what gets standardised, and what gets escalated, and building and managing an appropriately sized team as the work grows.

You'll act as the senior legal point person for product-related regulatory matters across the business.
Mews operates in regulated environments, which means product decisions carry real legal and regulatory weight, from AML, BSA, KYC and KYB obligations through to supervisory expectations, audits and market entry. The teams building these products need legal support that moves at their pace and helps them make sound decisions early, with repeatable operating discipline around them. Getting this right is what lets Mews scale regulated and non-regulated products confidently.
What you would do
Own the Product & Regulatory legal remit across Mews' SaaS and fintech environment, setting priorities, operating norms and the quality bar for legal support to Product and Engineering.
Embed with Product and Engineering as a hands-on product counsel, surfacing legal, regulatory and commercial trade-offs early and resolving them pragmatically across the release lifecycle.
Provide senior legal guidance on regulated product design, launch and scaling, including payments, embedded finance, money transmission, partner-bank and BaaS models, and cross-border propositions.
Build and manage a small specialist pod of counsel and paralegals, coaching them into strong product partners and building the playbooks, templates and working norms that let teams move faster without adding risk.
Use AI to reshape how legal support is delivered into product development, improving speed, quality and consistency across the pod.
AI Fluency Level 3: in this role that means going beyond using AI for your own drafting and analysis. You'll redesign how the pod delivers legal support to product, using AI across intake, issue-spotting, comparison and first-draft playbooks; build approaches the rest of the team can follow, including prompt quality and review discipline; and apply strong legal judgement about when AI output is incomplete, unreliable or too risky to rely on without deeper review.
For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to "AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates" on Confluence.
What you would bring
Significant in-house legal experience in technology, SaaS or fintech, with strong evidence of working closely with product teams rather than reviewing their work after the fact.
Strong fintech and regulatory exposure, ideally in payments, embedded finance or money transmission, including releasing regulated products and handling partner-bank or BaaS models.
Working knowledge of financial-crime regulation (AML, BSA, KYC, KYB) applied to product and operational decisions, plus experience with supervisory expectations, audits, investigations or regulatory change.
A hands-on builder mentality with clear examples of processes, guidance or tooling you've created, and sound commercial judgement that balances legal risk with business outcomes rather than defaulting to "no."
People-leadership experience, ideally managing lawyers and/or paralegals, and AI Fluency Level 3 or the equivalent hands-on experience using AI in day-to-day legal work.

Experience acting as true product counsel rather than purely commercial counsel.
Experience in earlier-stage or scaling environments rather than highly siloed large-enterprise settings.
Experience leading a regional or specialist legal team while staying close to product and business execution.

Sharp commercial instincts and strategic thinking, with a focus on driving business success while effectively navigating legal complexities. You are comfortable letting go of immaterial points to keep negotiations moving efficiently.

Trustpilot began in 2007 with a simple yet powerful idea that is more relevant today than ever — to be the universal symbol of trust, bringing consumers and businesses together through reviews. Trustpilot is open, independent, and impartial — we help consumers make the right choices and businesses to build trust, grow and improve.
Today, we have more than 350 million reviews and 60 million monthly active users across the globe, with 149 billion annual Trustpilot brand impressions, and the numbers keep growing. We have more than 1000 employees and we’re headquartered in Copenhagen, with operations in Amsterdam, Denver, Edinburgh, Hamburg, London, Melbourne, Milan and New York.
We’re driven by connection. It’s at the heart of what we do. Our culture keeps things fresh –– it’s built on the relationships we create. We talk, we laugh, we collaborate and we respect each other. We work across borders and cultures to be the universal symbol of trust in an ever-changing world. With vibrant office locations worldwide and over 50 nationalities, we’re proud to be an equal opportunity workplace with diverse perspectives and ideas.
Our purpose to help people and businesses help each other is a tall order, but we keep it real. We’re a great bunch of humans, doing awesome stuff, without fuss or pretense. A successful Trustpilot future is driven by you –– we give you the autonomy to shape a career you can be proud of. If you’re ready to grow, let’s go.

This role sits at the intersection of payments, digital assets and emerging payments technologies. You’ll help teams navigate a rapidly evolving legal and regulatory landscape, helping Monzo innovate responsibly while protecting our customers.
You’ll work at all levels in the organisation and with a wide-range of stakeholders from Product Managers and Designers, to Operations professionals and Software Engineers, and Risk, FinCrime and Compliance professionals.
While payments, digital assets and emerging financial technologies will be your primary focus, more broadly, you will also have opportunities to work within a team of product lawyers to give first rate legal advice and support to Monzo’s Product Collectives, including in areas like personal and business banking.
🔑You’ll play a key role by...
You’ll work directly with senior lawyers, product managers and engineers to provide legal advice and commercial insights to develop and grow Monzo Bank in the UK - and internationally.

Partner with product managers to advise on legal matters, in particular relating to the impact of digital assets and emerging financial technologies, and advise on the legal and regulatory requirements for Monzo.
Help to develop efficient ways of working to enable Monzo to scale quickly, and ensuring Monzo operates safely and in accordance with the law and regulation.
Provide training and knowledge sharing with other Monzonauts on the impact of laws and regulations for Monzo and our customers in your specialist area..
Often act as the sole lawyer advising product managers or other colleagues, identifying legal issues proactively, evaluating relevant risks and finding effective solutions to unique and complex business activities.
You’ll work closely and collaboratively with Monzo’s Director of Legal for Payments & Business Banking, Director of Product Legal, the General Counsel of Monzo Bank Limited and the other members of the UK Legal team to provide legal advice and commercial insights, in particular in relation to digital assets and other emerging financial technologies, to Product teams.
You’ll be a trusted advisor and will work proactively and collaboratively with other relevant stakeholders and teams across the Monzo Group, including the Product, Risk & Compliance, Supplier Operations, Financial Crime, Fraud and Operations teams.
You’ll advise on the evolving legal and regulatory framework for digital assets and emerging financial technologies, working with colleagues across the UK and EU to to help us identify relevant local legal and regulatory requirements and apply them to our products.
You’ll work with colleagues across the Legal and Board Governance Collective to improve the management of our teams’ activities, including through identifying suitable technology solutions to streamline workflows, optimise processes and efficiencies, and increase scalability.
You’ll proactively manage relationships with external suppliers and law firms to enhance processes around cost management to ensure we are optimising our spend and extracting best value while delivering top-quality legal support.
🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…
You are a technically excellent lawyer with a minimum of 5 years of relevant post-qualification experience, with recent experience of digital assets, emerging financial technologies and the evolving regulatory regime.
You have demonstrated experience of advising on laws and regulations relevant to financial services, including the UK regulatory regime as it applies to digital assets and emerging payment technologies.
You are a team player and a keen problem solver, skilled at assessing risk and recommending solutions that balance commercial and risk considerations. You think ahead, anticipate relevant challenges, understand the commercial objectives of the teams you support, set clear objectives, and find effective solutions.
You are proactive, take initiative to broaden your knowledge, and are passionate about the intersection of banking and technology and the transformation unfolding in consumer finance. You are excited to work in a fast-paced environment and to join us for the next stage of our journey at Monzo!

At Minnesota Cannabis Services, we’re not just building businesses — we’re building the people who make them great. Our team partners with leading operators across cultivation, manufacturing, distribution, and retail to deliver world-class expertise in legal, finance, analytics, marketing, HR, and technology.
We’re looking for professionals who take pride in their work, move with purpose, and thrive in fast-changing environments. The kind of people who hold themselves to high standards, think creatively, and find satisfaction in solving hard problems.
When you join our team, you’ll work alongside some of the most experienced leaders in the industry — professionals who share their knowledge freely and lead by example. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to take ownership of meaningful work that shapes the future of one of the fastest-growing industries in America.
The Opportunity
This is the senior-most attorney seat in our organization. You will own the legal and compliance function end to end: legal strategy, regulatory compliance, corporate structure, real estate and transactions, and risk management across everything we and our clients do.

You'll report directly to the CEO, work daily with a four-person executive team that decides fast and doesn't do bureaucracy, and help set the standard for a corporate office being built right now. The path to Chief Legal Officer is real and defined for the right candidate.
For the right candidate, the work itself is the draw: cannabis regulation is complex, fast-moving, and genuinely interesting, and this seat touches all of it — regulatory strategy, governance, leasing and land use, legislative affairs, lender relationships, licensure. Your first six months will have defined strategies and objectives, so you'll know exactly what you're walking into and exactly what success looks like.
What You'll Own
Regulatory compliance and audit-readiness across every market and license type we support — built and maintained to a standard that welcomes scrutiny. Own licensing applications, renewals, ownership-change requirements, and regulatory deadlines; work with market leaders to implement controls and close audit findings.
Contracts: personally draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements; establish review standards and approval processes; and ensure executed agreements, obligations, and notice and renewal dates are accurately maintained.
Corporate governance and structure: architect, draft, and implement entity and compliance frameworks in partnership with financial advisors.
Real estate and transactions: lease review, subleasing, and transactional work supporting turnkey construction and facility solutions for licensed operators.
Legal operations: own the use and administration of our Legal Ops platform and the processes around it, including intake, priorities, deadlines, document control, reporting, and escalation. Verify record accuracy, build repeatable workflows, and make the platform the team's source of truth.
Legal team leadership: directly manage and develop the in-house legal team, including a senior counsel and two paralegals. Set priorities, assign work, review deliverables, and hold the team accountable for accurate, timely execution, while directing outside counsel with tight control of scope and spend.
Government affairs: you must speak purple. Cannabis policy here advances through bipartisan relationships, and we work credibly with lawmakers and stakeholders across the political spectrum — Republicans and Democrats alike — as a matter of principle. If partisan politics would get in the way of our mission, you’re not the right candidate.
Other important responsibilities include zoning, land use, and municipal approvals; labor and employment partnership with Human Resources; and litigation readiness quarterbacking external counsel.
Who This Seat Fits
A senior attorney who builds and is deeply fulfilled by navigating complexity and responsibility. The balance here leans player over coach: you'll draft, negotiate, research, and file — and be proudest of the work you produce with your own hands.

You create clear ownership, reliable deadlines, and consistent review standards, and you develop junior staff to meet them. It fits someone energized by ownership, high standards, and particularly variety in their scope of work and expertise.

We want someone who practices at the modern frontier: we lead with AI and technology across the entire company, legal included, and genuine current fluency and mastery with AI legal tools is part of the job.
We're an in-person team by design — we believe presence is how mentorship, exceptional culture, and a corporate office actually get built — so this role is on-site in Edina, five days a week between the hours of 8:00 am - 5:00 pm.

$225,000–$250,000 and benefits. A defined path to Chief Legal Officer. Direct access to ownership and real decision-making authority. A modern, AI-forward legal practice. Relocation assistance for the right candidate. And a seat at the table in a nascent industry where the impact is still being influenced by people like you.

JD with active bar membership in good standing; Minnesota admission or ability to obtain promptly.
8+ years including senior in-house leadership, with demonstrated experience building or owning a legal or compliance function.
Deep multi-state regulatory experience in cannabis (strongly preferred) or a comparably regulated industry: alcohol, pharmaceuticals, gaming, tobacco, etc.
Demonstrated hands-on commercial contract drafting and negotiation, disciplined management of regulatory deadlines and records, and experience supervising and developing junior staff.
Multi-unit retail, franchising, or real estate depth is a plus.
Exceptional attention to detail, decisiveness, and the highest ethical standards.

Nebius is seeking a pragmatic and highly structured Senior Employment Counsel, to act as the primary legal partner to the HR team. The role will lead advice on employment and labour law (mostly Dutch) across the full employee lifecycle, including employment terms, compensation and benefits, performance and conduct matters, sickness and absence, investigations, reorganisations, terminations, settlement arrangements and employee disputes.
The role will also support Nebius's international growth by coordinating employment-law work in a wide range of new jurisdictions. This includes ensuring that compliant employment agreements, policies, templates and processes are established and maintained for each relevant country, in close partnership with HR, Compensation & Benefits, Compliance, the wider Legal team and external counsel.
Operating with a high degree of autonomy, the successful candidate will provide practical, business-oriented advice, manage sensitive matters with sound judgement and discretion, and build scalable ways of working in a fast-moving environment where structures, processes and priorities continue to evolve.

Act as the primary legal contact for the HR team (and other HQ units), providing timely, practical, decisive and commercially balanced advice on employment and labour law and employee-relations matters, and escalating material risks appropriately.
Advise across the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment terms, onboarding, employment status, performance, conduct, sickness and absence, investigations, disciplinary measures, terminations and post-termination obligations.
Manage employee (Labor) disputes and contentious matters from early assessment through resolution, including settlement negotiations, termination agreements, litigation or administrative proceedings, and coordination (consulting) with external counsel.
Advise on compensation and benefits matters, including salary and bonus arrangements, incentive and equity plans, allowances, pensions and changes to terms and conditions, in partnership with HR and Compensation & Benefits.
Draft, review, negotiate and maintain Dutch employment agreements, offer letters, policies, handbooks, settlement agreements, secondment and mobility documentation, and related templates.
Work directly with the Dutch Works Council ( ondernemingsraad ), advising on information, consultation and consent processes, preparing supporting documentation, assisting with meetings and ensuring timely follow-up and implementation.
Advise on reorganisations, restructurings, redundancies, business transfers and other workforce changes, including employee consultation, communications and implementation planning.
Lead employment-law workstreams for entry into new jurisdictions by identifying required local documents, policies, registrations and decision points; instructing and managing international external counsel for scope, quality and cost; and translating local advice into practical implementation steps.
Build and maintain scalable employment-law infrastructure, including global and local templates, country playbooks, launch checklists and approval workflows.
Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments, update agreements, policies and guidance, and provide training to HR, managers and other stakeholders.

A Dutch law degree or equivalent legal qualification, with a strong specialisation in employment and labour law.
At least 7 years of relevant post-qualification legal experience, with a substantial and recent focus on Dutch employment and labour law, gained in-house and/or at a reputable law firm.
Professional fluency in Dutch and English, both written and spoken.

The TLC oversees a transportation ecosystem that moves nearly 1 million riders every single day the equivalent of the entire Boston transit system. TLC is the agency responsible for regulating New York City's taxicab and for-hire vehicle industry.

With approximately 180,000 licensed drivers, 1,000 businesses, 115,000 vehicles including and the iconic yellow taxi at the heart of our city’s identity, TLC is entering a new era of dignity, accountability, and collaboration across the for hire vehicle sector.

TLC continues to be on the front lines of a rapidly changing mobility landscape and our innovative efforts--whether requiring minimum pay for app drivers, ensuring wheelchair accessible service, making our licensed fleet more environmentally sustainable, working to eliminate traffic fatalities, or preventing discriminatory service--often serve as a model for other cities.
In this New Era for TLC, the agency is guided by three core priorities:
· Driver and Passenger Dignity ensuring every interaction reflects respect and fairness
· Corporate Accountability holding regulated entities to consistent, transparent standards
· A Transportation System that Works Together equitable, modern, and accessible
The Prosecution Division investigates and prosecutes summonses issued by TLC which consist of administrative, field, and consumer-initiated complaints. The division prosecutes a wide range of violations including reckless driving, unlicensed operation, illegal street pickups, harassment, and leaving the scene of an accident.
The Prosecution Division investigates and prosecutes all summonses issued by TLC, which amounts to over 100,000 summonses each year.

Under the leadership of the Managing Attorney for Prosecution, and the direct supervision of the Senior Supervising Attorney, the Supervising Attorney of Adjudications (Hearings) Unit will assist the Senior Supervising Attorney in the daily management of the Hearings Unit and will assist in overseeing prosecuting attorneys assigned to appear on TLC summonses at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearing (OATH).
The Supervising Attorney will assist in the management of the prosecution of TLC summonses at OATH Hearings Division.

Responsibilities will include but are not limited to: managing weekly and daily calendar of TLC summonses; assigning and monitoring cases handled by prosecuting attorneys; overseeing the preparation of evidence and witnesses for introduction at administrative hearings; completing defaults list for distribution to OATH; collaborating with OATH to ensure the efficient disposal of cases; coordinating with TLC enforcement staff to ensure officer presence at required court appearances; providing instruction and feedback to prosecuting attorneys as needed; working with the Summons Integrity Committee to review directives, settlement offers, and summonses prior to issuance; and providing training to new and existing prosecutors assigned to the Hearings unit and Prosecution.

The NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) protects and enhances the daily economic lives of New Yorkers to create thriving communities. DCWP licenses nearly 45,000 businesses in more than 40 industries and enforces key consumer protection and workplace laws that apply to countless more.

By supporting businesses through equitable enforcement and access to resources, DCWP protects the marketplace from predatory practices and strives to create a culture of compliance. DCWP empowers consumers and working families by providing the tools and resources they need to achieve financial health and work-life balance.

DCWP also conducts research and advocates for public policy that furthers its work to support New York City’s communities.

For more information about DCWP and its work, call 311 or visit DCWP at NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), sign up for its newsletter, or follow on its social media sites, X, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.
Founded in 2014, the Office of Labor Policy & Standards (“OLPS”) enforces the City’s worker protection laws, including the Protected Time Off Law, Fair Workweek scheduling laws that protect fast food and retail workers, and Delivery Worker Laws that protect delivery workers classified as independent contractors.

OLPS settles and litigates dozens of large cases a year on behalf of classes of workers who have experienced violations of pay or scheduling rights. We have recovered over $120 million for workers through enforcement and raised pay by over $1 billion via the minimum pay rate for delivery workers classified as independent contractors.

We also administer the Freelance Isn’t Free Act (FIFA) program, which assists freelance workers who have experienced wage theft and other violations, and we bring pattern and practice litigation on behalf of freelancers against repeat violators.

Under all laws we enforce, OLPS obtains monetary compensation for workers for violations and brings companies into compliance.

Working closely with outside stakeholders, OLPS also advocates for new laws, performs research and data analysis to make policy recommendations, and conducts outreach and education to workers, employers, and the general public.

Under Mayor Mamdani, DCWP’s worker protection enforcement staff is rapidly expanding from a staff of 45 to 75 in 2026, with further expansion planned in future years. More information about our office is available at nyc.gov/workers.
